svg.title: Symmetry-breaking charge transfer in a perylene diimide dimer inside a six-helix bundle of a hexagonal DNA origami
svg.desc: A blueprint sketch of a hexagon with six spokes is filled in by the DNA origami, rod by rod. The origami is about 80 nm across and carries several PDI dimers, marked by dots. Zooming in on one, looking down the six-helix bundle that forms the edge, shows two perylene diimide (PDI) molecules stacked and slightly twisted in the hollow of the bundle. A second zoom into that hollow reveals the chemical structure of the two PDIs, which separate and untwist so each can be seen, with a linker that fades out toward the DNA. Their placement is encoded by the DNA. A photon excites the dimer, then the symmetry breaks: an electron transfers from one PDI to the other, leaving a positive charge on the first and a negative charge on the second.
